userStories.title: Media models and URL validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need typed models and URL validation so the rest of the feature works with clean data.
acceptanceCriteria: New package src/ninja_bot/media/ (with __init__.py) containing models.py
`MediaKind = Literal["mp3", "mp4"]`

Frozen dataclass VideoInfo: title, uploader (str|None), duration_s (int|None), thumbnail (str|None), webpage_url, view_count (int|None), upload_date (datetime.date|None), is_live (bool), is_playlist (bool)

`parse_info(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> VideoInfo` maps yt-dlp info dict keys (title, uploader, duration, thumbnail, webpage_url, view_count, upload_date as YYYYMMDD, is_live, _type == 'playlist') and tolerates missing keys
`format_duration(seconds: int | None) -> str` returns m:ss or h:mm:ss (65 -> '1:05', 3725 -> '1:02:05', None -> 'Unknown')
Exception classes in models.py: MediaError (base), InvalidUrlError, UnsupportedMediaError, TooLargeError, DownloadError; each carries a short user-facing message
`validate_url(text: str) -> str` in src/ninja_bot/media/planning.py strips whitespace, accepts only http/https URLs with a host, else raises InvalidUrlError
Unit tests: parse_info (full, minimal, playlist, live), format_duration, validate_url (valid, ftp://, no scheme, empty, whitespace-padded)

userStories.title: Download planning that fits the upload limit
userStories.description: As a user, I want the bot to automatically pick a quality that fits Discord's upload limit so my download isn't rejected for size.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure function `plan_download(info, kind, limit_bytes, max_duration_s) -> DownloadPlan` in src/ninja_bot/media/planning.py
DownloadPlan is a frozen dataclass exposing kind, limit_bytes, and either audio_bitrate_kbps (mp3) or an ordered height_ladder (mp4)
Raises UnsupportedMediaError when info.is_live, info.is_playlist, duration_s is None, or duration_s > max_duration_s
mp3: picks the highest bitrate from [192, 128, 96, 64] kbps where duration_s * kbps * 1000 / 8 <= limit_bytes; raises TooLargeError if even 64 kbps does not fit

mp4: height_ladder is [1080, 720, 480, 360, 240]; helper `format_selector(plan, height) -> str` returns a yt-dlp format string capping height, filtering by filesize<=limit / filesize_approx<=limit, merging video+audio and preferring mp4/m4a
mp4: raises TooLargeError up front only if the lowest rung cannot plausibly fit, using a documented conservative minimum-bitrate constant for 240p
Unit tests: each rejection case, bitrate selection at boundaries, TooLargeError for a very long mp3 at a small limit, format_selector output for each height
Typecheck passes
./scripts/check.sh passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy strict, pytest)

userStories.title: Info embed builder
userStories.description: As a user, I want an embed showing the video's key details alongside the file so I can see what was posted.
acceptanceCriteria: `build_embed(info: VideoInfo, kind: MediaKind) -> discord.Embed` in src/ninja_bot/media/embed.py

Fields: Uploader, Duration (via format_duration), Views (thousands-separated), Uploaded (YYYY-MM-DD); fields with missing data are omitted

Footer shows the chosen format ('MP3' or 'MP4')
Respects Discord limits (title <= 256, field values <= 1024) even for very long titles/uploader names

userStories.title: yt-dlp downloader wrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I need one isolated class that talks to yt-dlp so the rest of the code can be tested with a fake.
acceptanceCriteria: `Downloader` Protocol in src/ninja_bot/media/downloader.py with `async fetch_info(url) -> VideoInfo` and `async download(url, plan, workdir: Path) -> Path`
YtDlpDownloader is the only module importing yt_dlp; blocking calls run through asyncio.to_thread
fetch_info uses extract_info(url, download=False) with noplaylist=True, quiet=True, no_warnings=True, then parse_info; yt-dlp DownloadError becomes our DownloadError with a friendly message

Pure `build_ydl_options(plan, height, workdir)` returns options: mp3 uses 'bestaudio/best' + FFmpegExtractAudio postprocessor (preferredcodec mp3, preferredquality = plan bitrate); mp4 uses format_selector(...) with merge_output_format mp4; both set outtmpl inside workdir, noplaylist True, quiet True

download walks the mp4 height ladder (or the single mp3 bitrate), checks the real output file size against plan.limit_bytes, steps down one rung when too big, deletes leftover partial files between attempts, and raises TooLargeError when nothing fits
Unit tests (no network) for build_ydl_options for both kinds and for the ladder/step-down logic, using an injected stub for the yt-dlp call and temp files of known size
Typecheck passes
./scripts/check.sh passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy strict, pytest)

userStories.title: /download slash command (core flow)
userStories.description: As a server member, I want to run /download url:<link> format:<mp3|mp4> and get the file plus an embed in the channel.
acceptanceCriteria: src/ninja_bot/cogs/media.py defines a Media cog with app_commands command `download(url: str, format)`; `format` is optional, a dropdown of choices mp3 and mp4, default mp4
Cog takes a Downloader (default YtDlpDownloader) and max_duration_s via constructor so tests inject a fake; setup(bot) builds it from bot.config.max_duration_seconds

Flow: validate_url -> interaction.response.defer(thinking=True) -> fetch_info -> plan_download using interaction.guild.filesize_limit (fallback 10 * 1024 * 1024 without a guild) -> download into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory -> interaction.followup.send(embed=build_embed(...), file=discord.File(path))
validate_url failure is answered with an ephemeral message before deferring

Each MediaError subtype after deferring is answered via followup with a clear friendly message; TooLargeError and UnsupportedMediaError replies include the embed when info is available; unexpected exceptions are logged and answered with a generic message that leaks no internals
Temp directory removed in every outcome (success and each error path)
'ninja_bot.cogs.media' added to EXTENSIONS in src/ninja_bot/bot.py

Tests with a fake Downloader and fake Interaction cover: success mp4 (default), success mp3, invalid URL, each MediaError subtype, unexpected exception, guild limit vs no-guild fallback, temp dir cleanup
Add a note to progress.txt: 'needs manual check in Discord test server' (not verifiable by Ralph)
Typecheck passes
./scripts/check.sh passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy strict, pytest)

userStories.title: /download concurrency limit and cooldown
userStories.description: As the owner, I want downloads throttled so the homelab LXC isn't overloaded by concurrent or repeated requests.
acceptanceCriteria: The Media cog holds an asyncio.Semaphore(1) so only one download runs at a time; the semaphore is acquired after defer and released in every outcome
/download has a 30-second per-user cooldown via app_commands.checks.cooldown(1, 30)
A cog-level app command error handler catches CommandOnCooldown and replies ephemerally with the remaining seconds; other errors are logged and answered with a generic message
Tests: a second concurrent request waits until the first finishes (use asyncio events with the fake Downloader); the cooldown handler replies with the remaining time
Typecheck passes
./scripts/check.sh passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy strict, pytest)
